points.why: Names Fixes That Fail and explains how each reasonable sign-off led to rarer, bigger batches that made incidents worse and harder to diagnose.
Traces the reinforcing side-effect loop and calls the incident a delayed side effect, but omits the balancing loop where sign-offs actually reduce incidents.
Says each round of the fix feeds the problem and a fourth would repeat it, but does not explicitly project what a fourth does a few rounds out.
Recommends smaller, more frequent deploys, automated checks, feature flags and fast rollback, tracking batch size and time to identify the cause, and a time-boxed bridge for any DB review.
Moves to the pattern across all three incidents (and asks to verify the first two), the structure, and the belief that approvals feel safer without being safer.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly recommends against the fourth sign-off and allows only a scoped, expiring stopgap.
Blames no individual and says the people who added sign-offs weren't wrong.

notes: Claiming the loop has 'no minus signs' and is purely reinforcing misstates the structure, since the sign-offs do have a real short-term balancing effect on incidents.
